door_input_group.description: All rates are per EA (each door assembly). A door assembly includes both faces, all 4 edges, frame/jamb, and glass lite painting where applicable. Rates are expressed as fixed_time_minutes per EA or EA per hour. Complexity modifier (FAC_XDOR_COMPLEXITY) is the PRIMARY cost driver — all base rates assume single_slab baseline.

task_production_rates.name: Entry Walkway/Porch Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic sheeting over entry walkway/porch/stoop. ~14 sec per SF. Canvas for crew traffic, plastic for overspray containment. Limited scope — immediate entry area only, not full-elevation landscape.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkway within drip zone. Secured against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Canvas on crew traffic areas.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Taped at all edges. Non-slip surfaces on all traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Door Hardware Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all door hardware per hardware group: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, address numbers. Photograph layout before removal. Place in labeled bag. ~18 min per hardware group for standard door. Grand entry with additional hardware (knocker, mail slot, doorbell) handled by complexity modifier.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All hardware removed. Photographed. Bagged and labeled.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All hardware removed. Photographed. Bagged and labeled. Hinge mortises inspected for defects.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All hardware removed. Photographed with detail shots. Bagged and labeled. Mortises inspected. Hinge alignment marks documented.

task_production_rates.name: Weatherstrip Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Protect weatherstripping from paint contact. Friction-fit: pull out, store safely. Non-removable: push low-tack tape deep into gap with putty knife. ~10 min per door perimeter (~20 LF of weatherstrip contact). NEVER paint weatherstripping.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Stripping fully protected or removed. No paint contact risk.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Stripping fully protected or removed. Verified before prime/finish.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Stripping fully protected or removed. Verified and documented. No paint contact risk.

task_production_rates.name: Threshold/Sill Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply tape and plastic film over threshold/sill to catch drips. Extend to interior floor at door swing arc. ~5 min per door. Simple tape-and-plastic application.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete threshold coverage. Extended to interior door swing.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete threshold coverage. Taped at all edges.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete threshold coverage. Taped. Extended to full interior swing arc.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Lite Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape glass-to-frame edge with UV-resistant tape + apply HDPE static-cling masking film over glass area. ~12 min per door with glass lites (panel complexity baseline). Grand entry with sidelites/transom: complexity modifier drives time up significantly (30-60 min). This is per-door masking, not per-lite.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed at frame edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Tape sealed tight. No bleed-through risk at edges.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Liquid mask alternative for razor-sharp lines. Complete coverage with premium edge definition.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer with door-specific tips (310 for steel/fiberglass, 411 for wood). Install 60-mesh filter. Stage brushes for edge/detail work. Test spray pattern on cardboard. ~30 min per project setup. Per-project fixed time, not per-door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified on cardboard.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern at correct distance. Backup tips staged.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Equipment calibrated. Multiple test patterns. Backup tips and filters staged.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage brushes (angled sash 2.5 in, flat 2 in), paint pots, materials. Set up access equipment per access_type (typically ground level). ~15 min per project setup. Less setup than spray — no equipment configuration needed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Materials staged. Access equipment stable.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Materials staged and pre-mixed. Fresh brushes.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Materials mixed and strained. Premium brushes staged.

task_production_rates.name: Solvent Clean Steel Door
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Xylene/acetone wipe on all steel door surfaces (both faces, edges, frame). White rag verification test. Follow with TSP detergent wash and rinse. ~18 min per door. CRITICAL: bare ferrous metal must be primed same day. NEVER use on fiberglass — damages resin.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full solvent wipe. White rag test — no color transfer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full solvent wipe. White rag verification. Two-pass minimum.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full solvent wipe with two-pass verification. Documented clean per wipe test.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss/Scuff Sand Steel Door

QT3.notes: Even scuff with 120-150 grit. No glossy patches remaining.

QT4.notes: Full surface sand. Feather scratches to imperceptible transition. 300-grit finish on rust spots.

QT5.notes: Systematic sand with raking light inspection. Zero visible scratch marks. 300-grit feather on all imperfections.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Degloss steel door surfaces with 120-150 grit to create mechanical tooth. Feather rust spots with 300-grit. Both faces + 4 edges + frame/jamb. Single_slab baseline. QT5 adds raking light inspection and finer finish.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even scuff pattern. No glossy patches. Adequate tooth for topcoat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface sand. All scratches feathered. No glossy patches under raking light.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic sand. Zero visible scratch marks. All imperfections feathered to 300-grit smooth. DFT-compatible surface.

task_production_rates.name: Steel Door Dent Repair
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand dented area 80-grit, apply two-component body filler, finish-sand 240/300-grit. ~20 min average per door (conditional — most NC steel doors arrive undamaged). Time varies widely with extent of damage. Lead skill level required for flush finish.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible dents filled. Flush finish by touch.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All dents and dings filled. Sand to smooth flush. Raking light verify.
defect_tolerance.QT5: ALL imperfections including minor surface waviness filled. Perfect flush. DFT-compatible fill depth.

task_production_rates.name: Wash Fiberglass Door
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mild dish soap wash on all fiberglass door surfaces. Rinse thoroughly and allow to dry. ~12 min per door. NO hydrocarbon solvents (xylene, acetone, mineral spirits) — damages resin matrix. Includes drying wait time allocation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Surfaces clean. No residue. Dry before next step.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Surfaces clean. No residue. Fully dry. Inspected for contaminants.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Surfaces clean. White rag verification. Fully dry. Documented clean.

task_production_rates.name: Light Scuff Sand Fiberglass Door (Paint-Grade Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light 220-grit scuff on paint-grade smooth fiberglass to create adhesion profile. ~12 min per door. Do NOT sand textured stain-grade fiberglass — destroys wood-grain profile. Fiberglass is consistently smooth, fast scuff. Less time than wood sanding because no grain to open.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light scuff. Gloss broken on all surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform scuff. No glossy patches remaining.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic scuff under raking light. All surfaces dulled.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Wood Door

QT3.notes: Full surface sand 120-150 grit. Even scratch pattern. No glossy patches.

QT4.notes: Full surface sand with systematic coverage. Inspect all edges and panel profiles.

QT5.notes: Full systematic sand with raking light inspection. All surfaces including panel recesses and end grain.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand all wood door surfaces (both faces, 4 edges, frame/jamb) with 120-150 grit. Remove mill glaze, open grain. Orbital sander for flat faces, hand blocks for edges and profiles. Single_slab baseline — panel recesses add time via complexity modifier.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even scratch pattern. Mill glaze removed. No glossy patches.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface sand. No missed areas. Edges and profiles reached.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic sand with raking light. All surfaces including recesses and end grain.

task_production_rates.name: Fill Wood Door Defects

QT4.notes: Fill all defects > 1/16 inch. Sand flush. Raking light verify.

QT5.notes: Fill ALL defects > 1/32 inch. Glazing putty for micro-imperfections. Perfect flush.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fill nail holes, minor defects, and small damage with exterior-rated wood filler. Allow cure, sand flush 150-220 grit. ~10-22 min per door depending on QT — higher tiers require finer defect thresholds and more thorough inspection.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible defects filled. Flush to touch.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects > 1/16 inch filled. Sand flush. Raking light verify.
defect_tolerance.QT5: ALL defects > 1/32 inch. Glazing putty for nibs. Perfect flush. DFT-compatible.

task_production_rates.name: Tannin Knot Spot Prime (Wood)

QT3.notes: Spot prime visible knots. Complete seal over each knot.

QT4.notes: Spot prime all knots including small ones. Extended coverage around knot area.

QT5.notes: Spot prime all knots with extended perimeter. Verify seal after drying — re-coat if bleed-through visible.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply alkyd/shellac stain-blocking primer to visible knots on tannin-rich wood species (mahogany, cedar, redwood, fir). Per-knot application before full acrylic primer coat. ~10-18 min per door depending on knot count and QT inspection standard. Conditional on tannin-rich species.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible knots sealed. No bleed-through after dry.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All knots sealed including small ones. Extended coverage. No bleed-through.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All knots sealed with extended perimeter. Verified seal after dry. Zero bleed-through.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Wood Panel Joints

QT3.notes: Caulk visible gaps at panel joints. Clean tooled bead.

QT4.notes: Caulk all panel joints. Uniform bead. Clean tool lines.

QT5.notes: Caulk all joints with precision tooling. Zero visible ridges after sanding. Full cure.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply flexible paintable caulk to wood door panel joints. Exterior-rated acrylic latex caulk. ~12-20 min per door (panel complexity). Applies only to wood panel/grand_entry doors — steel/fiberglass panels are factory-sealed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible gaps sealed. Clean tooled bead.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All joints caulked. Uniform bead. Clean lines.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All joints with precision tooling. Zero ridges. Sanded smooth.

task_production_rates.name: Dust Removal After Prep
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth all door surfaces including panel recesses, edges, and frame. Zero dust contamination before primer/finish. ~5 min per door. Quick task after sanding operations.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All surfaces tack-clothed. No visible dust.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All surfaces including recesses tack-clothed. No dust under raking light.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete tack-cloth. White-glove test. Zero contamination.

task_production_rates.name: Spray DTM Primer — Steel Door Faces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray DTM primer on both steel door faces with 310 tip. Even wet coat per manufacturer mil spec. ~15 min per door (both faces). Spray is fast on flat steel surfaces. CRITICAL: prime same day as surface prep — bare ferrous metal rusts within hours.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even wet coat. No holidays. Target 1.5 mils DFT.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even wet coat. No holidays. Uniform mil build. Inspect edges.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Even wet coat. No holidays. DFT verified with gauge. Zero missed spots.

task_production_rates.name: Brush DTM Primer — Steel Door (Faces/Edges)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush DTM primer on steel door faces and all 4 edges. Angled sash for faces, flat brush for edges. ~30 min per door. Brush is ~2x slower than spray for door faces but covers edges in same pass. Same-day prime after prep.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No drips. Complete coverage of faces and all 4 edges.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No drips. Complete six-surface coverage. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Even coat. No drips. Complete coverage. DFT spot-check.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Acrylic Primer — Fiberglass/Wood Door Faces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray 100% acrylic latex primer on fiberglass or wood door faces. 411 tip for wood, 310 for fiberglass. Even wet coat. ~15 min per door (both faces). 100% acrylic MANDATORY for fiberglass — no oil/alkyd. Wood doors: this covers faces only when spray; edges covered by TSK_XDOR_PRIME_EDGES.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even wet coat. No holidays. 100% acrylic ONLY on fiberglass.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even wet coat. No holidays. Uniform mil build.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Even wet coat. DFT verified. Zero holidays.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Acrylic Primer — Fiberglass/Wood Door (Faces/Edges)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush 100% acrylic primer on fiberglass/wood door faces, all 4 edges, and frame/jamb. Angled sash for faces and panel recesses, flat brush for narrow edges. ~30 min per door. Covers all surfaces in single pass (no separate edge task needed). 100% acrylic MANDATORY for fiberglass.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No drips. Complete six-side coverage for wood.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. Complete coverage. No holidays. Edges inspected.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Even coat. Complete six-side coverage. DFT spot-check.

task_production_rates.name: Prime All Door Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush prime all 4 door edges (top, bottom, hinge, latch) with substrate-appropriate primer. Runs when faces are sprayed — edges always brushed. Bottom edge is critical moisture entry point on wood. Prop door open during bottom edge cure. ~12 min for 4 edges (flat brush 2 in).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete edge coverage. No drips on faces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete edge coverage. Prop door for bottom edge cure. Clean edge-to-face transition.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full edge coverage. Bottom edge prop. DFT check on edges.

task_production_rates.name: Six-Side Seal Verification (Wood)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify all six sides of wood door have received primer: both faces, top, bottom, hinge edge, latch edge. Mirror inspection for bottom edge. ~5 min per door. Lead skill — warranty critical. Failure to seal = warranty voidance.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visual verify all 6 sides primed. Bottom edge confirmed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Flashlight inspect all edges. Mirror for bottom edge. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full six-side inspection with mirror and raking light. DFT spot-check on primer.

task_production_rates.name: Spray First Finish Coat — Door Faces

QT3.notes: Even coat, no runs or sags. Clean edges. Standard acrylic enamel.

QT4.notes: Even coat with premium material. Inspect for holidays, runs, sags before tipping off.

QT5.notes: Spray in controlled environment (door removed to shop). Fine tip pattern. Even wet film. DFT monitoring.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray first finish coat on both door faces. 310 tip for steel/fiberglass, 411 for wood. Single_slab baseline. Do NOT back-roll on metal doors. For panel doors: spray flat areas between brushed recesses. QT5 may use controlled environment.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No runs, sags, or holidays. 6-foot visual acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No defects under raking light at 3 feet.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Zero defects at arm's length under raking light. Uniform DFT.

task_production_rates.name: Brush First Finish Coat — Door Faces

QT3.notes: Even coat. Long even strokes. No lap marks.

QT4.notes: Even coat with premium material. Tip off brush marks while wet.

QT5.notes: Brush technique for zero visible marks. Long even strokes. Foam pad tipping.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush first finish coat on both door faces with angled sash brush (2.5 in). Brush technique: vertical strokes (steel/fiberglass) or follow grain (wood). Maintain wet edge to avoid lap marks. ~28-45 min per door depending on QT. Brush is ~2x slower than spray for faces.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No lap marks. Clean edges.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No brush marks under raking light at 3 feet. Tipped off while wet.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Zero visible brush marks at arm's length. Foam pad tipping for final smoothness.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Panel Recesses — First Finish Coat

QT3.notes: Complete recess coverage. No puddles in corners.

QT4.notes: Thin even coat in recesses. No buildup at panel-to-stile transition.

QT5.notes: Precision brush work. Zero buildup, zero holidays. Raking light verify before dry.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat into panel recesses on raised panel doors. Sequence: panels first, then stiles, then rails. Prevents lap marks. Angled sash brush. ~15-25 min per door (panel baseline). Grand entry with more panels handled by complexity modifier.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete recess coverage. No puddles or drips.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Thin even coat. No buildup at transitions.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision detail. Zero buildup. Uniform film in all recesses.

task_production_rates.name: Brush All Door Edges — First Finish Coat

QT3.notes: Complete edge coverage. No drips on faces.

QT4.notes: Complete coverage including hinge mortises. Clean edge-to-face transition.

QT5.notes: Full edge coverage. Hinge mortises. Edge-to-face blend. Prop door for bottom edge cure.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush first finish coat on all 4 door edges with flat brush (2 in). Edges ALWAYS brushed regardless of face method. Bottom edge: apply paint, prop door open during cure. ~10-15 min per door for 4 edges.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete edge coverage. No drips or sags on faces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Hinge mortises covered. Clean transitions.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage. Mortises filled. Prop door. DFT-compatible build.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Mullions/Sidelite Frames — First Finish Coat

QT3.notes: Complete mullion coverage. Clean glass-to-mullion line.

QT4.notes: Precision mullion work. No paint on glass. Sharp lines at masking edge.

QT5.notes: Exacting mullion detail. Razor-sharp lines. Uniform film build on all profiles.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush first finish coat on sidelite/transom mullions, muntin bars, and frame sections on grand entry assemblies. Detailed brush work in tight profiles between glass lites. Lead skill required. ~20-35 min per grand entry assembly. Only activates for grand_entry complexity.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete mullion coverage. Clean glass-to-mullion line.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Precision mullion work. No paint on glass. Sharp masking lines.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Exacting detail. Razor-sharp lines. Uniform film on all profiles.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Inspection

QT3.notes: Visual scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays.

QT4.notes: Raking light inspection. Mark all defects. Check panel recesses for buildup.

QT5.notes: Raking light + DFT gauge spot-check. Zero tolerance for defects. Document findings.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Inspect first finish coat for runs, sags, drips, holidays, orange peel, dust nibs. QT3: quick visual. QT4: raking light. QT5: raking light + DFT. Single_slab baseline. ~5-12 min per door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visual scan. Major defects identified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Raking light scan. All defects marked.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Raking light + DFT. Zero defects. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Sand

QT4.notes: Light scuff sand with 220-grit. Even scratch pattern. No aggressive sanding.

QT5.notes: Hand-sand 220/320-grit in raking light. Feather all repairs to imperceptible transition.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light scuff sand between finish coats for intercoat adhesion. QT3: NOT performed — visual inspect only. QT4: light 220-grit. QT5: 220 + 320-grit in raking light. ~18-25 min per door (single_slab baseline, both faces + edges).

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light scuff. Gloss broken. Even scratch pattern.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic hand-sand. 320-grit finish. All repairs feathered imperceptibly.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Defect Repair

QT4.notes: Sand out runs/sags. Spot-coat holidays.

QT5.notes: Full defect repair. Glazing putty for nibs. Feather all repairs. Re-inspect.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Repair defects found during intercoat inspection. Sand out runs/sags, spot-coat holidays. QT5: glazing putty for dust nibs. ~8-15 min per door. Conditional — only if defects found during inspection.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Runs/sags sanded smooth. Holidays spot-coated.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All defects repaired. Feathered imperceptibly. Glazing putty for nibs.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth all surfaces after intercoat sanding. Zero contamination before second finish coat. ~5 min per door. Runs after intercoat sand (QT4/QT5 only).

defect_tolerance.QT4: All surfaces tack-clothed. No dust.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete tack-cloth. White-glove verify. Zero contamination.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Second Finish Coat — Door Faces

QT3.notes: Even coat, no runs or sags. Final visual.

QT4.notes: Even coat with premium material. Raking light before dry.

QT5.notes: Final coat. May spray with door hanging for gravity leveling. Zero defects.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray second finish coat on both door faces. Same technique as coat 1. QT5: final coat may be applied with door re-hung for gravity leveling on vertical faces. Single_slab baseline.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No runs, sags, or holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coat. No defects under raking light.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Zero defects at arm's length. Uniform DFT. Gravity-leveled film.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Second Finish Coat — Door Faces

QT4.notes: Even coat. Tip off brush marks while wet.

QT5.notes: Zero brush marks. Foam pad tipping for final smoothness.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush second finish coat on both door faces. Same technique as coat 1. Maintain wet edge. Single_slab baseline.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coat. No lap marks.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No brush marks under raking light. Tipped off.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Zero visible marks at arm's length. Foam pad tipped.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Panel Recesses — Second Finish Coat

QT4.notes: Thin even coat. No buildup at transitions.

QT5.notes: Precision detail. Zero buildup. Uniform film build.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush second finish coat into panel recesses. Same sequence as coat 1: panels first, stiles, then rails. Single_slab baseline (panel door minimum).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. No puddles.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Thin even coat. No buildup.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision detail. Uniform film in all recesses.

task_production_rates.name: Brush All Door Edges — Second Finish Coat

QT3.notes: Complete edge coverage. Prop door for bottom edge cure.

QT4.notes: Complete coverage. Clean transitions. Prop door.

QT5.notes: Full edge coverage. Hinge mortises. Prop door 24-48 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush second finish coat on all 4 edges. Prop door open during 24-48 hr cure for bottom edge. Same technique as coat 1.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete edge coverage. Prop for bottom cure.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Clean transitions. Propped.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage. Mortises. 24-48 hr prop.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Mullions/Sidelite Frames — Second Finish Coat

QT3.notes: Complete mullion coverage. Clean glass-to-mullion line.

QT4.notes: Precision mullion work. Sharp masking lines.

QT5.notes: Exacting detail. Razor-sharp lines. Uniform film.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush second finish coat on sidelite/transom mullions and frames. Same technique as coat 1. Grand_entry only.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Clean glass-to-mullion line.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Precision work. Sharp masking lines. No paint on glass.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Exacting detail. Razor-sharp lines. Uniform film.

task_production_rates.name: Hardware Reinstallation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Reinstall all door hardware from labeled bags using pre-removal photographs: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, address numbers, knocker, mail slot. ~18 min per hardware group. Verify each component positioned and functional.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All hardware reinstalled. Correct positions. Functional test.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All hardware reinstalled. Alignment verified against photos. Full function test.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision reinstall using documented alignment marks. Full function test. No paint on hardware finish.

task_production_rates.name: Weatherstrip Reinstallation & Check
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Re-insert friction-fit weatherstripping or remove protective tape from non-removable stripping. Verify seal compression around full perimeter. Check for paint contamination. ~8 min per door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Stripping seated. Perimeter compression. No paint contamination.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Stripping seated. Full perimeter compression verified. No contamination.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Stripping seated. Full compression. Zero contamination. Documented seal check.

task_production_rates.name: Door Operation Test
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Test complete door operation: open/close smoothly, latch engages, deadbolt throws, strike plate alignment, no binding. Verify bottom edge clearance over threshold. ~5 min per door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Open/close. Latch. Deadbolt. No binding.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full operation test. Verify alignment. Check bottom clearance.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Comprehensive test. All hardware function. Bottom edge cure check. Prop instructions to homeowner.

task_production_rates.name: Final Door Inspection

QT3.notes: Visual scan for defects. Mark touch-ups.

QT4.notes: Raking light inspection. All surfaces. Glass masking line quality.

QT5.notes: Raking light + DFT verification (target 3.0-5.0 mils total). Zero-defect standard. Document final DFT.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final visual inspection of completed door: both faces, all 4 edges, panel recesses, mullions (grand_entry), glass masking lines. Mark touch-up areas. Lead skill required. Single_slab baseline.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visual scan. Major defects flagged at 6 feet.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Raking light scan at 3 feet. All defects flagged.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Raking light at arm's length. DFT verified. Zero-defect standard.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Minor Defects

QT4.notes: Address all marked defects. Feather into surrounding area.

QT5.notes: Address every defect. Invisible feather. Re-inspect after touch-up.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch up minor defects found during final inspection: holidays, edge drips, glass masking bleed-through. Brush touch-up with matching finish. Feather into surrounding. ~5-15 min per door depending on QT.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects addressed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All marked defects addressed. Feathered into surrounding.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Every defect addressed. Invisible repair. Re-inspected.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Masking Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove glass masking film and tape from all glass lites. Remove tape at angle to prevent paint film lifting. Clean adhesive residue from glass. ~8 min per door with glass. Grand entry with sidelites/transom takes longer — handled by complexity modifier.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Masking removed. Glass clean. Paint line verified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Masking removed at angle. Adhesive cleaned. Sharp paint line.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision removal. Razor-clean glass. Razor-sharp paint line. Micro-bleed cleaned.

task_production_rates.name: Threshold Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove threshold tape and plastic protection. Clean any drips from threshold surface. ~3 min per door. Simple teardown.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean removal. No adhesive residue. No paint drips.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Clean removal. Threshold finish verified undamaged.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Clean removal. Threshold finish verified. No residue.

task_production_rates.name: Walkway Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove canvas drop cloths and plastic from entry walkway/porch. Fold paint-side-in. ~9 sec per SF. Faster than setup — just pick up and fold.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Fold paint-side-in. Walkway clean.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Fold paint-side-in. Walkway inspected for drips.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Fold paint-side-in. Walkway clean. No paint residue.

task_production_rates.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean all brushes, spray equipment (flush lines, clean tip, filter). Proper brush cleaning for reuse (~5,000 LF lifespan). Flush airless with water for latex. ~25 min per project. Per-project fixed time, not per-door.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment cleaned. Brushes stored properly.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment cleaned. Brushes shaped and stored. Spray lines flushed.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Equipment cleaned. Brushes shaped. Spray lines flushed and stored. Documented.

factor_modifiers.description: Door complexity modifier — PRIMARY cost driver. Applied to all per-door (EA) task rates. All base rates in task_production_rates are calibrated to single_slab baseline.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: All EA-based task rates (all tasks except FIXED and SF-based walkway tasks)
factor_modifiers.notes: Single_slab (flush door, no glass, no panels): 1.00 baseline. Panel (raised panels, glass lites, recesses): 1.60x — adds panel recess brush time, glass masking time, and caulk joint time. Grand_entry (sidelites, transom, mullions, multiple glass lites, additional hardware): 3.50x — substantially more masking, detail brush work, mullion painting, and hardware management. Grand_entry is the combination of panel complexity PLUS sidelite/transom scope. Applied as: effective_time = base_time x modifier. Baseline single_slab total: ~90-120 min. Panel: ~145-190 min. Grand_entry: ~315-420 min (5-7 hrs).
factor_modifiers.max_stacking_note: Multiplicative with FAC_QT, FAC_XDOR_SUBSTRATE, FAC_EXT_ACCESS. See stacking cap check.

factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier modifier — controls pace, scrutiny level, and defect tolerance. Applied via qt_rates structure for qt_scaled tasks; this modifier is for tasks that use a single base rate across tiers.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: Binary tasks that have uniform rates across tiers (protection, cleanup, equipment setup). qt_scaled tasks use qt_rates instead — this modifier does NOT double-stack with qt_rates.
factor_modifiers.notes: QT3: production pace, 6-foot visual. QT4: slower pace, 3-foot raking light. QT5: meticulous pace, arm's length lighted inspection. Applied as: effective_time = base_time x modifier.

factor_modifiers.description: Door substrate material modifier — affects prep time and primer type. Applied to prep and prime tasks.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: Prep tasks (solvent clean, degloss, sand, fill) and prime tasks. Does NOT apply to finish coat tasks — primed surface is normalized.
factor_modifiers.notes: Steel: baseline (solvent clean + degloss + dent fill). Fiberglass: 0.90 (simpler prep — wash + light scuff, no sanding or filling). Wood: 1.10 (six-side seal requirement, grain filling, tannin spot prime, panel joint caulking). Substrate-specific tasks already activate/deactivate by applicability rules — this modifier adjusts the common tasks that run across substrates.

factor_modifiers.description: Exterior access type modifier — replaces FAC_HEIGHT for exterior elevation work. Most entry doors are ground level; elevated entries (raised porch/deck) may require ladder.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: All labor tasks at elevation. Does NOT apply to ground-level protection setup or FIXED per-project tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per Exterior_Modifiers_Doctrine.md §2. Most exterior doors are at grade (ground = 1.00). Ladder modifier applies for elevated deck/raised porch entries. Scaffold and lift rarely applicable to door painting specifically. Applied as: effective_time = base_time x modifier.

factor_modifiers.description: Exterior substrate state modifier for prep task rate adjustments. Driven by SS_EXT_* input state.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: Prep tasks only. Prime modifier: SS_EXT_BARE_METAL = 1.10, all others = 1.00. Finish modifier: always 1.00 — prep normalizes the surface.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per Exterior_Modifiers_Doctrine.md §3.2. Bare metal gets 1.20 prep modifier (rust management, solvent clean overhead). Factory-primed gets 0.80 (less prep needed — just scuff and clean). Field-primed gets 0.90 (minimal re-prep). Applied as: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier.

factor_modifiers.description: Wind condition modifier — spray and masking tasks only.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: Spray application tasks (TSK_XDOR_*SPRAY*) and masking tasks (TSK_XDOR_GLASS_MASK). Does NOT apply to brush tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per Exterior_Modifiers_Doctrine.md §4. High wind excludes spray tasks entirely — flag for re-scope. Moderate wind adds 25% overhead for masking stability and drift management.

factor_modifiers.description: Sun exposure modifier — finish coat tasks only.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: All finish coat application tasks. Does NOT apply to prep or protection tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per Exterior_Modifiers_Doctrine.md §5. Full sun compresses working window (flash dry, blistering risk on dark colors). Full shade slows cure. Applied as time increase.

factor_modifiers.description: Surface temperature modifier — prime and finish coat tasks.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: All prime and finish coat application tasks. Does NOT apply to prep or protection tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per Exterior_Modifiers_Doctrine.md §6. Cold surface (< 50F) slows cure and risks adhesion. Hot surface (> 85F) causes flash dry and streaking. Especially critical for dark door colors on steel substrate (thermal mass).

modifier_stacking_check.formula: total_modifier = FAC_XDOR_COMPLEXITY x FAC_QT x FAC_XDOR_SUBSTRATE x FAC_EXT_ACCESS x FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION x FAC_EXT_WIND x FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE x FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP

worst_case_scenarios.scenario: Grand entry, QT5, wood, ladder, bare wood, light breeze, full sun, hot surface
worst_case_scenarios.resolution: Grand_entry modifier (3.50) is the dominant factor. When stacking exceeds 4.0x, the engine applies the 4.0x cap. In practice, grand_entry + QT5 already = 4.55x which exceeds the cap, so environmental modifiers are absorbed. The 4.0x cap represents the upper bound for fixed-price estimation. For grand_entry + QT5 scenarios, flag for hourly or T&M pricing review.
worst_case_scenarios.recommendation: Grand entry QT5 doors should be flagged for manual review and potential hourly pricing. The 4.0x cap protects against unreasonable fixed-price estimates.

worst_case_scenarios.scenario: Panel, QT5, wood, ground, bare wood, calm, partial shade, optimal
worst_case_scenarios.notes: Common high-tier scenario. Well within 4.0x cap.

worst_case_scenarios.scenario: Single slab, QT3, steel, ground, factory primed, calm, partial shade, optimal
worst_case_scenarios.notes: Fastest scenario — factory-primed steel slab at QT3. Below baseline (factory prime reduces prep).

time_totals_by_scenario.description: Estimated total time per door for common scenarios. Sums applicable task fixed_time_minutes. Complexity modifier applied to per-EA tasks.

scenarios.name: Single slab, steel, factory-primed, spray, QT3
scenarios.breakdown: Walkway + hardware remove (18) + weatherstrip (10) + threshold (5) + equip setup spray (30) + solvent clean (18) + degloss (22) + dust (5) + finish spray face x2 (30) + finish edge x2 (20) + inspect intercoat (5) + hardware reinstall (18) + weatherstrip reinstall (8) + op test (5) + final inspect (5) + touchup (5) + threshold teardown (3) + walkway teardown + tool clean (25) = ~105 min minus walkway SF tasks
scenarios.notes: Excludes prime module (factory-primed). No glass masking (single slab). No intercoat sand (QT3). Walkway protect/teardown is SF-based, not included in per-door total.

scenarios.name: Panel, wood, bare, spray, QT4
scenarios.notes: Includes all prep (sand, fill, tannin spot, caulk), prime, 2 finish coats with panel recess work, intercoat sand at QT4, glass masking. Complexity modifier 1.60x on per-EA tasks.

scenarios.name: Grand entry, wood, bare, spray, QT5
scenarios.notes: Maximum scope: all prep, prime, 2 finish coats, panel + mullion work, glass masking, intercoat sand QT5. Grand_entry 3.50x on per-EA tasks. Hits the upper end of 5-10 hr range from research. Grand_entry QT5 flagged for manual review.

quality_effects.description: Production pace. Visual inspection at 6 feet. No intercoat sanding. Standard acrylic enamel. Single_slab: ~90-120 min total.
quality_effects.interstage_labor: Inspect only — no sand, no repair, no dust removal.
quality_effects.inspection_level: Quick visual scan for obvious defects.

quality_effects.description: Slower pace. Raking light inspection at 3 feet. Intercoat sand 220-grit between finish coats. Premium acrylic enamel. QT4 adds ~15-30% time over QT3.
quality_effects.interstage_labor: Full cycle: inspect + sand 220 + repair + dust removal.
quality_effects.inspection_level: Systematic raking light scan at 3 feet.

quality_effects.description: Meticulous pace. Lighted critical inspection at arm's length. Intercoat hand-sand 220/320-grit. DFT verification. Premium acrylic enamel. Door may be removed for controlled environment painting. QT5 adds ~30-50% time over QT3.
quality_effects.interstage_labor: Full cycle: inspect + hand-sand 220/320 + repair with glazing putty + dust removal.
quality_effects.inspection_level: Raking light + DFT gauge at arm's length. Zero-defect standard.
quality_effects.special_conditions: QT5 doors may be removed from hinges for shop painting. Final coat may be applied with door re-hung for gravity leveling.

assumptions.value: ~90-120 min total per door (single_slab, spray, bare substrate, QT3)
assumptions.source: User brief; Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md §4; sibling spec rates
assumptions.note: Base rates calibrated to single_slab flush door with no glass. All task times are for this baseline. Complexity modifier scales total time for panel and grand_entry.

assumptions.value: 3.50x complexity modifier for grand_entry (user brief range: 3.00-5.00x)
assumptions.note: User brief specified 3.00-5.00x range. Used 3.50x as middle-ground — grand_entry adds sidelite/transom scope but not a full doubling of every task. Field calibration needed. Grand_entry + QT5 scenarios should be flagged for hourly pricing review.

assumptions.value: 1.60x complexity modifier for panel doors (user brief range: 1.50-1.75x)
assumptions.note: User brief specified 1.50-1.75x. Used 1.60x as calibrated value — panel doors add recess brush work, glass masking, and caulk joints but share the same face spray/brush task structure.

assumptions.value: Brush face painting takes approximately 2x the time of spray face painting
assumptions.note: Spray face: ~15 min QT3. Brush face: ~28 min QT3. Ratio is ~1.87x. Brush method is slower but eliminates spray equipment setup (30 min) and overspray management. For single doors, brush may be more time-efficient overall.

assumptions.value: Equipment setup and tool cleaning are per-project FIXED time, not per-door
assumptions.note: Equipment setup (spray or brush) and tool cleaning happen once per project regardless of door count. All other tasks scale with door count (EA).

risks.topic: Grand entry QT5 exceeds 4.0x stacking cap
risks.description: Grand_entry (3.50) x QT5 (1.30) = 4.55x before any environmental modifiers. Exceeds the 4.0x stacking cap, meaning the engine will cap at 4.0x which may underestimate actual time.
risks.mitigation: Flag grand_entry + QT5 combinations for manual review and potential hourly/T&M pricing. The 4.0x cap protects against runaway estimates but may need human override for these scenarios.

risks.description: TSK_XDOR_DENT_FILL_STEEL has a wide range (10-45 min) because damage extent is unpredictable. Most NC doors arrive undamaged, but shipping damage can require extensive repair.
risks.mitigation: Rate represents average case. Extreme damage should trigger site assessment and hourly scope for dent repair.

risks.topic: Glass masking time for grand_entry is highly variable
risks.description: Grand entry glass masking depends on number and complexity of sidelites/transom lites. Base rate assumes standard grand entry configuration; exotic configurations may exceed estimates.
risks.mitigation: Complexity modifier (3.50x) accounts for most variation. Extreme configurations (e.g., full glass sidelites with multiple divided lites) should be assessed individually.
